encounters.cc: Sharp, intermittent right-sided lower abdominal and pelvic pain

lines: Sharp, intermittent right-sided lower abdominal and pelvic pain
The 28-year-old with PCOS and iron deficiency anemia returns for prenatal care of pregnancy with fetal gastroschisis.

She reports a 5-day history of sharp, intermittent right-sided lower abdominal and pelvic pain that worsens with sudden movements and when changing positions, and that the pain sometimes radiates to her right groin and vaginal area.
She denies vaginal bleeding, contractions, or urinary symptoms.
Her prenatal course has been uncomplicated so far, and she is otherwise healthy.
- Laparoscopic right ovarian cystectomy (corpus luteum hemorrhage, age 24)
- Prenatal vitamin (high-dose folic acid) 1 tablet PO daily (containing folate 4mg)
- Ferrous sulfate 325mg (65mg elemental iron) PO daily
- Paternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retail store manager.
On examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender except for mild discomfort on deep palpation over the right lower quadrant.
The uterus is palpable at the level of the umbilicus, consistent with gestational age, and there is no cervical dilation.
The clinician suspects that her symptoms are due to stretching of a specific pelvic structure associated with the expanding uterus.

encounters.cc: Recent changes in her appearance including facial hair growth and acne

lines: Recent changes in her appearance including facial hair growth and acne
The patient is a 31-year-old with polycystic ovary syndrome who returns for continued prenatal care following her recent evaluation for dyspnea.
She presents with her husband, concerned about recent changes in her appearance.
She reports a significant increase in facial hair growth, deepening of her voice, and acne over the past two months.
She denies any visual changes, headaches, or abdominal pain.
- Myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and hydrocephalus (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated thus far.
- Laparoscopic right ovarian cystectomy (corpus luteum hemorrhage, age 24)
- Prenatal vitamin (high-dose folic acid) 1 tablet PO daily (containing folate 4mg)
- Ferrous sulfate 325mg (65mg elemental iron) PO daily
- Paternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retail store manager.
Her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute
On physical examination, she appears well.
She has noticeable facial hirsutism and temporal balding.
Her laboratory tests are as follows:
- Total testosterone: 150 ng/dL (normal non-pregnant female range: 15-70 ng/dL)
- Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS): 180 µg/dL (normal non-pregnant female range: 35-430 µg/dL)
Pelvic ultrasound reveals bilateral, multicystic ovarian masses measuring 3 cm on the right and 4 cm on the left.
There are no signs of fetal distress or abnormalities.
